title: Choose the visual world for brickbot.ro (round 4)
question: Every card now keeps the content you pinned: the wordmark, the motto, one main photo, two buttons. Only the world around them changes.

options.label: Curved-Crease Shell
options.lineage: curved-crease paper folding: one sweeping arc lifts a flat sheet into a rigid shell
options.thesis: Brick by brick, as engineering: one black sheet folded along a single yellow arc into a structure, with the team photo held on the curved face.
options.viewport: Pinned by you: BRICKBOT wordmark + “We build our future brick by brick!” + one main photo + main and secondary buttons. The photo sits on a panel curved by one sweeping yellow arc; the wordmark runs along the crease, the motto below, buttons at the foot of the arc.
options.risk: Quiet and elegant rather than electric: it may read too calm for a teen team.

raised.raise: Exactly three coordinated colours on the first screen: black, #FFEC17, burgundy.
One full-frame inversion as the single motion moment.

options.label: Event Display
options.thesis: The team photo is the collision point: yellow tracks burst out of it through detector rings, and the wordmark, motto and buttons are pinned to the tracks like readouts.
options.viewport: Pinned by you: BRICKBOT wordmark + “We build our future brick by brick!” + one main photo + main and secondary buttons. A circular crop of the Nationals celebration sits at the centre-right as the collision; yellow tracks curl out across the screen. A giant wordmark rides one track, and the motto and buttons are pinned as readouts.
options.case: Beats the shell on both axes: it is electric and STEM at once (the brand's lightning, made literal as energy tracks), and the photo stays the focal point.
options.risk: Busy if too many tracks; the motion must be one burst on load, then calm.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: theatre cyclorama lit from night to day
options.thesis: Build our future, staged as a dawn: the cyc rises from black through burgundy into brand yellow behind the team, who stand cut out against it.
materials: a cut-out team in front of the cyc
options.viewport: Pinned by you: BRICKBOT wordmark + “We build our future brick by brick!” + one main photo + main and secondary buttons. A huge wordmark sits low across the yellow horizon band, the team stands in front, and the motto and two buttons are set in stencil caps like a lighting cue sheet.
options.case: A strong metaphor for “our future”, and dramatic. It's competitive on clarity, but the gradient world is less distinctive.
options.risk: Gradients can look like a generic sunset wallpaper.

options.label: Fan Shrine
options.thesis: The site as the shrine the team would build for itself: tiled bolt background, the wordmark as a banner, animated dividers, a visitor counter.
options.viewport: Pinned by you: BRICKBOT wordmark + “We build our future brick by brick!” + one main photo + main and secondary buttons. A centred column on a tiled lightning background, the wordmark banner glowing, the photo framed in a bevel, and two chunky buttons. A blinking 'you are visitor No. 15996' at the foot.
options.case: Maximum teen personality. It loses on how seriously a national sponsor will take it.
options.risk: It can read as a joke rather than a team that went to Worlds.

options.label: Portrait Plate
options.thesis: Full-length portrait on a flat painted backdrop.
options.viewport: A full-length figure on a flat backdrop.
options.case: Needs a new photoshoot; the existing photos are crowds.

options.label: Datamatics
options.case: No colour, so no #FFEC17, and no people.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark robotics-team site done well: big photo hero, stats row, latest season, sponsor strip.
canonCard.viewport: A full-bleed photo, a headline with two buttons, and a stats row under it.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other FTC team site, which is the problem the brief named.
